Are the profiles real? — Statistical validation

Each profile's defining behaviour, measured straight from the raw data (no AI, no clustering) and compared to the average player. Cohen's d ≥ 0.8 is "large", ≥ 2.0 is "very large"; all are significant at p < 0.05.

ProfileDefining behaviourvs. average Cohen's dp-valueVerdict
Fighter penalty-double rate ×1.31 2.13 0.016 ✓ strong
Insurance Player partscore rate ×1.24 3.30 0.004 ✓ strong
Slam Hunter slam rate ×1.37 2.81 0.004 ✓ strong
NT Specialist NT rate ×1.27 4.62 0.004 ✓ strong
Honest note: charts 1 & 3 partly re-describe how the groups were defined (we picked the most extreme players, so of course they look extreme). The genuinely independent evidence is chart 2's side-habits plus this validation table. The "Insurance Player" group is the weakest of the four (only ×1.24), so we describe it carefully.

The visualizations

1 · Each profile spikes on its own behaviour

Four habits — bidding big (slam), playing safe (partscore), fighting opponents (penalty double), preferring NT. Each mini-chart picks one habit and shows how much every group does it. In every chart one group clearly stands out — and it is named after that habit.

2 · The fingerprint of each profile

One row per group, one column per behaviour. Red = does it more than average, blue = less. The strong red square on each row is the group's own habit. The other coloured squares are side-habits we did NOT select for — that coherence is the real evidence the groups are genuine.

3 · How the players split up

Left: most players (83%) are 'average'; the special types are small groups at the edges. Right: each special group vs. the average player, with a '×' showing how many times more they do their signature habit.

4 · The risk line: bold vs. careful

Every dot is one player. Right = more risk (slams), up = more caution (stops low). No separate islands — one big cloud with the special types at the edges. This is the main finding: a smooth continuum, not boxes.

5 · Fighters vs. NT-lovers

Chart 4 separates two of the four types; this one separates the other two. Right = fights opponents more (penalty doubles), up = prefers NT contracts. Fighters drift right, NT Specialists drift up.
